value.linkage: alpha-(1->4) glucan backbone; one residue is one alpha-D-glucopyranosyl unit
value.end_groups: none counted; yeast-GEM writes the species as ONE residue, C6H10O5, with no terminal water, which is the per-repeat-unit convention the repeat-unit surrogate route requires
value.convention_note: The GEM species is ONE alpha-1,4-linked glucose residue. The shipped table priced it instead from the BiGG accession's structure, which is the four-residue oligomer C24H42O21, giving -1127.249 kJ/mol in the cytosol and -1370.874 in the vacuole, about 4.6x the residue value. The residue energy here is the same dimer-difference construction the mannan record uses: R = [G(maltose) - G(H2O)] / 2, with maltose the alpha-1,4 dimer, evaluated at each compartment's own conditions.

preferred_dimer_difference.rule: a disaccharide is two residues plus one water, so R = [G(alpha-1,4-maltose) - G(H2O)] / 2

searches.query: accession-priced metabolites whose structure formula differs from the GEM formula
searches.outcome: glycogen s_0773 and s_0774 priced from C24H42O21 against the GEM's C6H10O5

decomposition_check.error: the repeat unit carries two attachment points, which the group decomposer refuses; the dimer and the monomer both decompose, which is what makes the difference construction available
